basic_information.name: Bolt.new
basic_information.creator: StackBlitz Inc. (founded 2017 by Eric Simons and Albert Pai; headquartered in San Francisco, USA)
basic_information.description: Bolt.new is an AI-powered web development platform that lets users prompt, run, edit, and deploy full-stack applications entirely in the browser, powered by StackBlitz's WebContainers technology. Often called the poster child of 'vibe coding', Bolt.new went from $0 to $20M ARR in just 2 months after launching in October 2024, making it the second-fastest-growing product in history after ChatGPT. For entrepreneurs, Bolt.new eliminates the traditional barrier between idea and working prototype: describe your app in natural language and get a deployable full-stack application in minutes, including frontend, backend, and database, with one-click deployment to Netlify. The platform reached 5 million signups and $40M ARR within 5 months.
basic_information.release_date: October 3, 2024 (initial launch via a single tweet; mobile app support added February 2025; built-in hosting and custom domains added August 2025)

technical_capabilities.underlying_models: Primarily Anthropic Claude models. The official platform offers two agents: v1 Agent (legacy) and Claude Agent. Under Claude Agent, users can select Claude Haiku 4.5 (lightweight/fast tasks), Claude Sonnet 4.5 (everyday coding), Claude Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.6 (deeper reasoning, architectural decisions). The open-source fork bolt.diy supports 19+ providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, Groq, xAI, Ollama, and more.
technical_capabilities.customization_depth: prompt-only | code-extension. Users interact via natural language prompts to build and modify applications. Advanced users can directly edit the generated code in the in-browser editor, use file locking to protect specific files from AI modifications, and employ targeted editing to constrain AI changes to specific sections. The open-source bolt.diy version allows deeper customization including self-hosting and model swapping.
technical_capabilities.api_access: No dedicated REST API for external programmatic use of the platform itself. Projects generate standard web applications with their own APIs (e.g., Express endpoints). GitHub integration allows exporting code for external development.
technical_capabilities.deployment_options: Cloud-hosted platform (bolt.new SaaS), one-click deployment to Netlify, built-in Bolt hosting with custom domain support (since August 2025), export to GitHub for local/external development, Netlify and Vercel deployment support. The open-source bolt.diy can be self-hosted via Docker or run as an Electron desktop app.
technical_capabilities.ai_model_flexibility: single-provider (official platform: Anthropic Claude only) | multi-provider (bolt.diy open-source: 19+ providers including BYOM via Ollama). On the commercial Bolt.new platform, users are limited to Anthropic's Claude model family but can choose between tiers (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus). For broader model flexibility, bolt.diy supports OpenAI, Google Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Groq, Cohere, Together AI, Perplexity, HuggingFace, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

user_experience.target_user: business_user | designer | developer | student. Bolt.new explicitly targets both professional developers seeking productivity acceleration and non-technical users ('next billion developers') including product managers, founders, marketers, and designers. Many users have never written code before. The platform is designed to be approachable by anyone who can describe what they want in natural language.
user_experience.learning_curve: minutes. Bolt.new is designed for immediate productivity: describe your app in plain language and get a working prototype in under 30 minutes. Benchmark tests show Bolt.new produces a working prototype in approximately 28 minutes, faster than competitors Lovable (35 min) and Replit (45 min).
user_experience.setup_time: 2-5 minutes from signup to first working demo. No local installation required: everything runs in the browser via WebContainers. Sign up, type a prompt, and a running application appears in the live preview panel.
user_experience.collaboration_features: Project sharing via URL, GitHub integration for version control and team collaboration. Teams plan supports multi-member access at $30/member/month. Enterprise plan includes SSO, dedicated manager, and compliance features. Version history and project forking available.
user_experience.template_library: Bolt.new supports specifying frameworks and libraries in prompts (e.g., 'build with Astro, Tailwind, and ShadCN'). The platform includes starter templates and the community shares prompt templates. Bolt.diy offers 15+ starter templates for popular frameworks. The platform auto-scaffolds projects with appropriate tooling (Vite, Next.js, React, etc.) based on the prompt.
user_experience.visual_builder_type: natural-language | code-editor. Primary interaction is through natural-language chat prompts that generate full-stack applications. Users can also directly edit code in the in-browser IDE with live preview. No drag-and-drop visual builder; the interface is a split-pane with chat on one side and a full code editor + live preview on the other.

ai_and_rag_capabilities.rag_support: No built-in RAG pipeline. Bolt.new generates applications rather than hosting AI reasoning. However, users can prompt Bolt to build applications that incorporate RAG functionality using libraries like LangChain, vector databases, and embedding APIs. Supabase integration provides database and auth capabilities that can support RAG app backends.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.agent_capabilities: single-step | multi-step. Bolt.new operates as an AI coding agent that can autonomously handle the complete app lifecycle: scaffolding, installing dependencies, writing code, running the dev server, debugging errors from the terminal and browser console, and deploying. The AI agent can iterate on errors it encounters. However, it is not a multi-agent system and does not orchestrate multiple independent AI agents.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.model_selection: Single-vendor with tier selection (official platform). Users select from Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, or Opus 4.6 depending on task complexity and budget. Different models consume tokens at different rates. Bolt.diy (open-source) provides full multi-vendor model selection with BYOM support.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.prompt_management: No formal prompt versioning or optimization features. Users interact through a conversational chat interface. Prompts are stored as part of the project conversation history. Community resources provide prompt engineering tips specific to Bolt.new (e.g., specifying frameworks, breaking requests into smaller steps). File locking and targeted editing help manage AI behavior.

integration_and_ecosystem.key_integrations: Netlify (deployment, 1M+ sites deployed), Supabase (databases, auth, file storage), GitHub (version control, code export), Expo (mobile app development), Firebase (backend services), Figma (design import), Stripe (payments), Name.com (custom domains). Built-in hosting with custom domain support since August 2025.
integration_and_ecosystem.integration_count: 8-10 official deep integrations. The platform focuses on quality over quantity: each integration (Netlify, Supabase, GitHub, Expo, Firebase, Figma, Stripe, Name.com) is tightly integrated into the workflow rather than offering hundreds of shallow connectors.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_support: Partial. Bolt.diy (open-source version) supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for enhanced AI tool calling. The official Bolt.new platform can work with MCP servers (e.g., Apple Docs MCP) but native MCP support details are limited.
integration_and_ecosystem.webhook_support: No native webhook triggers for the platform itself. However, applications built with Bolt.new can include webhook and API endpoints as part of their backend code (e.g., Express.js routes, API endpoints).
integration_and_ecosystem.export_formats: Full source code (downloadable/pushable to GitHub), deployed web application (Netlify, Bolt hosting), mobile application (via Expo), shareable project URL. Code is standard web technology (React, Next.js, Vite, etc.) with no proprietary format, ensuring portability.

pricing_and_accessibility.pricing_model: freemium | credit-based (token-based). Free tier available with monthly token allowance. Paid plans scale by token allocation. Tokens are consumed by AI model interactions; different models (Haiku vs. Opus) consume at different rates.
pricing_and_accessibility.free_tier_limits: Free plan: ~1 million tokens per month, daily limit of 300K tokens per day. Includes access to the AI-powered app builder, live preview, and instant hosting on a free Bolt URL (bolt.new subdomain). Tokens do not roll over. Sufficient for experimenting and building 2-5 small projects per month.
pricing_and_accessibility.paid_plans: Pro $20/month: 10M tokens/month. Pro 50 $50/month: 26M tokens/month. Pro 100 $100/month: 55M tokens/month. Pro 200 $200/month: 120M tokens/month. Teams $30/member/month: 26M tokens per member. Enterprise: custom pricing with SSO, compliance, dedicated manager, training. Annual subscriptions get 10% discount. Paid tokens roll over for one additional month (since July 2025).
pricing_and_accessibility.open_source: open-core. The commercial Bolt.new is proprietary. The open-source version bolt.diy (MIT license) is the official community fork, originally called 'oTToDev' and 'bolt.new ANY LLM'. Note: bolt.diy source code is MIT-licensed, but the WebContainers API requires a commercial license for production/commercial usage. Prototypes and POCs do not require a commercial license.
pricing_and_accessibility.self_hosting_option: Not available for the official Bolt.new platform (cloud-only SaaS). Self-hosting is available via bolt.diy (open-source fork) using Docker or direct machine installation. Self-hosted bolt.diy is free to run (infrastructure costs only), and users own the runtime, logs, and data. Electron desktop app available for local usage.
pricing_and_accessibility.data_residency_and_sovereignty: StackBlitz is a US-based company. Per StackBlitz privacy policy, personal information may be stored and processed in the United States and other countries. No explicit EU data residency option for the commercial platform. No specific GDPR compliance certification documented for Bolt.new. For data sovereignty needs, bolt.diy self-hosted with local models (via Ollama) provides full control. No EU AI Act readiness certification as of early 2026. [uncertain]

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the vibe coding / AI app builder category. Bolt.new is widely recognized as the poster child of the 'vibe coding' movement. It was the second-fastest-growing product in history after ChatGPT, reaching $4M ARR in 30 days and $20M ARR in 2 months. Forecasting $100M ARR by end of 2025. Competes directly with Lovable, Replit, and Vercel v0 as a top-tier AI coding platform.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Primarily prosumers, indie developers, and startup founders rather than named enterprise customers. Over 1 million websites deployed via Bolt + Netlify partnership (as of March 2025). 5 million registered users by March 2025. User base spans developers, product managers, founders, marketers, and designers. Enterprise features (SSO, compliance, dedicated manager) suggest growing enterprise adoption, though specific enterprise customer names are not publicly disclosed.
adoption_and_market.community_size: GitHub: bolt.new repo has 16.2K stars, 14.6K forks, 163 watchers, 15 contributors (MIT license). bolt.diy (open-source fork) has ~15K+ GitHub stars with an active contributor community. 5 million+ registered users (March 2025). 1 million+ monthly active users. Active Discord community via StackBlitz Discord server. Over 1 million AI-generated websites deployed on Netlify.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: ~$135M across 3 rounds. Latest: $105.5M Series B (closed January 23, 2025) at a $700M valuation, led by Emergence Capital and GV (Google Ventures), with Madrona Venture Group, Conviction, and Mantis participating. Previous investors include Greylock, Flex Capital, and Tribe Capital. Revenue trajectory: $0 to $4M ARR in 30 days (October 2024), $20M ARR by December 2024, $40M ARR by March 2025, forecasting $100M ARR by end 2025. StackBlitz was near shutdown in late 2023 (only $80K annual revenue) before Bolt.new's explosive success.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: Lovable (fastest European startup growth, $20M ARR in 2 months, strong full-stack capabilities), Vercel v0 (best for existing developers, tightest developer workflow integration), Replit (most feature-rich and powerful, but feels more developer-oriented), Cursor/Windsurf (IDE-based AI coding, more traditional developer tools). Bolt.new differentiates through: (1) WebContainers technology enabling full Node.js environment in the browser with zero local setup, (2) fastest time to working prototype (~28 min benchmark), (3) seamless Netlify deployment partnership, (4) open-source fork (bolt.diy) for self-hosting and model flexibility.
adoption_and_market.ecosystem_lock_in_risk: low. Generated code is standard web technology (React, Next.js, Vite, TypeScript) with no proprietary format. Full code export to GitHub. Deployable to any hosting provider (Netlify, Vercel, or custom servers). The only lock-in factor is the conversational context/project history within Bolt.new, which is lost if you move to external development. Bolt.diy provides a fully open-source alternative.

teaching_and_classroom.class_project_idea:
Project 1: 'AI-Powered Startup Landing Page & MVP' (60 min) - Students sign up for Bolt.new free tier, then prompt the AI to build a complete landing page for their startup idea with: hero section, value proposition, pricing table, contact form, and a functional feature (e.g., a simple calculator, quiz, or recommendation engine). Students iterate through 3-4 prompt refinements to add Tailwind CSS styling, responsive design, and Supabase backend for form submissions. They deploy to Netlify with one click. Deliverable: live URL of their startup landing page + 2-minute pitch analyzing how long this would have taken with traditional development (weeks) vs. Bolt.new (1 hour), and what the implications are for startup speed-to-market.

Project 2: 'From Idea to Full-Stack App in 45 Minutes' (45 min) - Students are given a business scenario (e.g., 'Build a simple CRM for a freelancer' or 'Create a task management app for a small team') and must use only natural language prompts to build a working app with Bolt.new. The app must include: user-facing frontend, at least one interactive feature, and a Supabase database for data persistence. After building, students present their app and analyze: (1) What worked well vs. what the AI got wrong, (2) Estimated cost to build this traditionally vs. with AI, (3) What are the limitations for scaling this to a real product. This project demonstrates the power and limits of vibe coding for entrepreneurial prototyping.

teaching_and_classroom.student_prerequisites: nothing. Bolt.new is designed for users with zero coding experience. Students only need a browser and an idea. Basic prompting skills help (knowing how to give clear, specific instructions to an AI), but the platform guides users through the process. Understanding what a website/app is conceptually is sufficient.
teaching_and_classroom.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & No-Code Tools) - primary fit. Students experience 'vibe coding' firsthand, building a working web application from natural language prompts. Also relevant to Session 3 (Framing & Managing AI Projects) for Build vs Buy analysis and understanding AI-assisted prototyping timelines, and Session 4 (AI Business Models & Strategy) for discussing how tools like Bolt.new change startup cost structures and time-to-MVP.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Bolt.new is ideal for pre-seed to seed-stage startups (1-5 person teams) who need to validate ideas fast. Best suited for: (1) Rapid prototyping and investor demos - build a working MVP in hours instead of weeks to show investors or test with early users; (2) Non-technical founders - solo founders or business-oriented teams who can describe their product but cannot code it can get a working version immediately; (3) Landing pages and marketing sites - spin up professional sites with forms, analytics, and payment integration for early customer acquisition; (4) Internal tools and dashboards - quickly build admin panels, CRM tools, or data dashboards that would otherwise require a developer hire. Less suitable for: complex enterprise applications, high-performance systems, or products requiring deep custom backend logic. The free tier is generous enough for initial prototyping, and the $20/month Pro plan supports sustained development.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_mvp: Minutes to hours. A basic landing page or simple web app: 15-30 minutes. A full-stack application with database, auth, and multiple pages: 2-4 hours. A more polished MVP with Supabase backend, Stripe payments, and Netlify deployment: 1-2 days of iterative prompting. Benchmarks show Bolt.new averages 28 minutes to a working prototype, faster than Lovable (35 min) and Replit (45 min). Compared to traditional development (4-12 weeks for a comparable MVP), Bolt.new compresses timelines by 10-100x.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Bolt.new when: you need a working prototype fast for validation or fundraising, your team lacks frontend/backend developers, you want to iterate rapidly on UI/UX with natural language instead of code, or you need a low-cost path to a deployable web application. Transition away from Bolt.new when: your application needs complex custom backend logic, you require fine-grained performance optimization, your codebase grows beyond what the AI agent can manage coherently, or you need enterprise-grade reliability. The ideal pattern is: start with Bolt.new for MVP, export code to GitHub, then bring in developers to scale and harden the codebase. Cost comparison: Free tier for initial prototyping; $20-50/month covers most startup prototyping needs; traditional development (hiring a freelancer or agency) for a comparable MVP would cost $5,000-50,000.
key_lessons: 1. Vibe coding is for validation, not production (yet): Bolt.new excels at getting from zero to working prototype faster than any traditional approach. Use it to validate your idea, test with users, and demo to investors. But plan to involve real developers when scaling to production, as AI-generated code often needs refactoring for maintainability, security, and performance.

2. Prompt engineering is your new technical skill: The quality of your Bolt.new output depends entirely on how well you describe what you want. Be specific about frameworks (Tailwind, React, Next.js), break complex features into sequential prompts, and use file locking to protect working code from being overwritten. This is a skill worth teaching to every entrepreneur.

3. Export early, own your code: Bolt.new generates standard web code (React, TypeScript, Node.js) that runs anywhere. Push to GitHub early and often. This ensures you are never locked in, and your code remains portable whether you continue with Bolt.new or transition to traditional development.

4. The cost structure has changed forever: What previously required a $50K development budget and 3 months of work can now be prototyped for $0-50 in an afternoon. This fundamentally changes startup economics: you can validate 10 ideas for the cost of one traditional prototype. The bottleneck shifts from 'can we build it?' to 'should we build it?'

5. Know the limits to avoid frustration: Bolt.new struggles with very large codebases, complex state management, and applications requiring deep backend architecture. If your prompts start producing inconsistent results or breaking existing features, it is time to export the code and continue with a human developer or a code-centric AI tool like Cursor.

confidence.data_quality: High. Information sourced from official Bolt.new documentation, Bloomberg, Netlify press releases, verified ARR figures from multiple business analysis sources, and the GitHub repository. Pricing and feature details confirmed across multiple independent sources.
confidence.cross_reference: Bloomberg (funding/valuation), Netlify press release (1M deployed sites), Growth Unhinged and The Split (ARR figures), StackBlitz GitHub (stars/license), Bolt.new support docs (pricing/features), multiple independent reviews (Prismetric, CodeItBro, Trickle, UXPilot, UI Bakery)
confidence.caveats: Bolt.new is evolving very rapidly: pricing tiers, token limits, and supported models change frequently. The platform launched only in October 2024, so long-term reliability and enterprise readiness are not yet proven. The $700M valuation and $40M ARR figures are from early 2025 and may have changed. GDPR/data residency information for the commercial platform is sparse. Performance comparisons (28 min to prototype) depend on use case complexity and may not be representative. The open-source bolt.diy has different capabilities and limitations from the commercial platform.
